old: Trigger, all must hold: the PR adds or widens two test units (TEST_CASE, SECTION, GENERATE arm, template instantiation), or one new unit plus one it widens; both make the same production call as the operation under test; both feed it the same GENERATE list or named constants, the same token or size set and the same source value type; both reach the same leaf branches of a function the diff changed. A commit that answers several gap items at once raises the priority of its units. A comment claiming "covers N cases" is a separate nit.

Procedure: name the production call of each unit. Follow it to the leaf function with branches the diff changed and map every input (each GENERATE value, each token index) to the arm it reaches. Simulate the unit's write order: a slot counts as observed only if no later write in the same unit replaces it before an assertion reads it. Record for each unit the set of (branch, slot, reference, precision, read path) its assertions observe. Compare pairwise, among the triggered units and any pre-existing unit on the same call that the PR widened with new assertions.
new:
Procedure:
1. Name the production call of each unit.
2. Follow it to the leaf function with branches the diff changed and map every input (each GENERATE value, each token index) to the arm it reaches.
3. Simulate the unit's write order: a slot counts as observed only if no later write in the same unit replaces it before an assertion reads it.
4. Record for each unit the set of (branch, slot, reference, precision, read path) its assertions observe.
5. Compare pairwise, among the triggered units and any pre-existing unit on the same call that the PR widened with new assertions.

old: Trigger, all parts: a sentence in the PR body, a README hunk or a comment hunk has a CI subject ("CI", "the required checks", "the build job", "the nightly", a workflow name), asserts a setting or coverage (a CMake option, a preset, a platform feature, "AMX-on/off"), and is not about a build the author made (a named tree, machine or runtron arm is a measurement statement). Also a reviewer comment that cites a workflow file:line as proof of what gates the PR, and a PR number offered as the date a setting changed.

Procedure: list every file under `.github/workflows` and the keys of its `on:` block. For every file with none of `push`, `pull_request` or `merge_group`, find its callers and quote the caller's `if:` gate. Find every place the setting lives (`.github`, `nix/`, `flake.nix`, `CMakePresets.json`, `CMakeLists.txt` default, `GNUmakefile`, README.ci.md) and name each hit's consumer: a workflow `run:` line belongs to that job; a nix file belongs to the job whose `nix build` recipe imports it; a preset belongs to whatever runs it. Get the gating set from `gh pr checks N --required` on a finished run (no row in progress or queued) and record each job's workflow name. Date the setting per file with `git log -S` and map the commit to its PR.
new:
Procedure:
1. List every file under `.github/workflows` and the keys of its `on:` block.
2. For every file with none of `push`, `pull_request` or `merge_group`, find its callers and quote the caller's `if:` gate.
3. Find every place the setting lives (`.github`, `nix/`, `flake.nix`, `CMakePresets.json`, `CMakeLists.txt` default, `GNUmakefile`, README.ci.md) and name each hit's consumer: a workflow `run:` line belongs to that job; a nix file belongs to the job whose `nix build` recipe imports it; a preset belongs to whatever runs it.
4. Get the gating set from `gh pr checks N --required` on a finished run (no row in progress or queued) and record each job's workflow name.
5. Date the setting per file with `git log -S` and map the commit to its PR.

old: Trigger: always. Cost: one `git log`, one `git show` per commit and one grep of `BASE:FILE` per hunk. Highest priority when a commit's author differs from the PR author, when a commit message or the body cites another PR number or says "folded", "stacked" or "fast-forward", when a commit subject starts with Name, Rename, Brace, Clean up, Shorten, Clarify, Reword or Tighten, or when a commit adds tests after a review round.

Procedure: write the identifier set: every backticked type, function, constant or Note title in "What changes", plus every name declared at namespace or class scope in a file the diff creates, minus any name that exists at BASE. Confirm each with `grep -c` over the diff. Bin commits: SIDE when the subject starts with one of the verbs above, or the commit changes only tests or comments, or its author is not the PR author; MAIN-FEATURE when the subject contains an identifier from the set verbatim; otherwise SIDE. Scan the hunks of every non-merge commit, SIDE first; a MAIN-FEATURE commit can carry a side hunk. A hunk is a candidate when at least half of its removed lines exist verbatim at BASE, at least one of them is not blank, brace-only or comment-only, and its added lines contain no PR identifier. A candidate in the same function or TEST_CASE as a hunk that carries an identifier inherits that hunk's status.
new:
Procedure:
1. Write the identifier set: every backticked type, function, constant or Note title in "What changes", plus every name declared at namespace or class scope in a file the diff creates, minus any name that exists at BASE. Confirm each with `grep -c` over the diff.
2. Bin commits: SIDE when the subject starts with one of the verbs above, or the commit changes only tests or comments, or its author is not the PR author; MAIN-FEATURE when the subject contains an identifier from the set verbatim; otherwise SIDE.
3. Scan the hunks of every non-merge commit, SIDE first; a MAIN-FEATURE commit can carry a side hunk.
4. A hunk is a candidate when at least half of its removed lines exist verbatim at BASE, at least one of them is not blank, brace-only or comment-only, and its added lines contain no PR identifier.
5. A candidate in the same function or TEST_CASE as a hunk that carries an identifier inherits that hunk's status.

old: Procedure: find global definitions by walking the header with a namespace depth counter and reporting added lines at depth zero that are not blank, comments or directives. Count includers: direct (files under h, src, t, bin, ingest whose `#include` names it) and transitive (closure over `#include` lines); report "N direct, M transitive of T". Classify the hunk's origin: owner-authored PR; fast-forward fold (`gh api repos/<org>/<repo>/commits/<sha>/pulls` lists another PR and the commit sits on the first-parent line with no merge commit of that PR); merge; side commit. Read every PR comment on the file by an owner and class it: placement accepted (names the symbol or the header and says keep, fine, agree, LGTM, go ahead), diagnosis agreed, or wording only. Only the first counts; an APPROVED review by an owner at a head that contains the hunk also counts. A comment counts only if its `commit_id` contains the introducing commit (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`). Use dates only to say that a reply cites a commit older than the thread it answers.
new:
Procedure:
1. Find global definitions by walking the header with a namespace depth counter and reporting added lines at depth zero that are not blank, comments or directives.
2. Count includers: direct (files under h, src, t, bin, ingest whose `#include` names it) and transitive (closure over `#include` lines); report "N direct, M transitive of T".
3. Classify the hunk's origin: owner-authored PR; fast-forward fold (`gh api repos/<org>/<repo>/commits/<sha>/pulls` lists another PR and the commit sits on the first-parent line with no merge commit of that PR); merge; side commit.
4. Owner set: authors of the file at BASE by recency, plus every requested reviewer of the PR with a commit on the file (map logins to authors with `gh api users/<login>`, then by email local part).
5. Read every PR comment on the file by an owner and class it: placement accepted (names the symbol or the header and says keep, fine, agree, LGTM, go ahead), diagnosis agreed, or wording only. Only the first counts; an APPROVED review by an owner at a head that contains the hunk also counts.
6. A comment counts only if its `commit_id` contains the introducing commit (`git merge-base --is-ancestor`). Use dates only to say that a reply cites a commit older than the thread it answers.
